controls.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
controls.summary: APIs expose endpoints that handle object identifiers without verifying the caller is authorized for that object (IDOR).
implementationChecklist: Validate object ownership on every request

controls.title: Broken Authentication
controls.summary: Authentication mechanisms are implemented incorrectly, allowing attackers to assume other identities.

controls.title: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
controls.summary: Excessive data exposure or mass assignment — object properties are returned or accepted without authorization.
evidenceExamples: Mass assignment / excessive data exposure findings

controls.title: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
controls.summary: APIs do not limit the resources a client can consume, enabling DoS and cost amplification.
evidenceExamples: Missing rate-limit findings (runtime confirmation often needed)

controls.title: Broken Function Level Authorization
controls.summary: Missing or improper authorization checks let users access functions beyond their privilege level.

controls.title: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
controls.summary: Business flows are exposed without compensating controls against automated abuse.

controls.title: Server Side Request Forgery
controls.summary: The API fetches a remote resource from a user-supplied URI without validation.

controls.title: Security Misconfiguration
controls.summary: Missing hardening, permissive CORS, verbose errors, or unpatched components across the API stack.

controls.title: Improper Inventory Management
controls.summary: Deprecated, undocumented, or non-production API versions remain exposed.
evidenceExamples: Requires API inventory / discovery, not SAST

controls.title: Unsafe Consumption of APIs
controls.summary: Data from third-party APIs is trusted and processed without adequate validation.
implementationChecklist: Apply the same input rules to third-party data
evidenceExamples: Unsafe deserialization / injection of upstream data findings
